record.paper_title: Stellar models: firm evidence, open questions and future developments
record.original_question: How can stellar evolutionary models provide a robust physical treatment of the third dredge-up in Thermally Pulsing Asymptotic Giant Branch stars by correctly describing convection and mixing across regions with strong composition and opacity discontinuities, so that the efficiency of the third dredge-up does not have to be represented by arbitrary methods and tunable free parameters?

evidence.quote: Concerning the 3DU, in spite of its fundamental relevance in determining the chemical enrichment of TPAGB star envelopes, its treatment in stellar evolutionary code is quite uncertain. This is due to the fact that we are not yet able to properly describe convection inside the stars, and in particular, in case of mixing occurring in a region with a strong composition/opacity discontinuity.

Many different - arbitrary - methods can be envisaged to treat the occurrence of the 3DU, but each one of these approaches has no robust physical ground. This has the important implication that in all fully evolutionary AGB models, the efficiency of the 3DU is managed by using one (or more) free parameter(s).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the theory of stellar evolution, a Thermally Pulsing Asymptotic Giant Branch (TPAGB) star is a low- to intermediate-mass star (initial mass roughly 0.8–8 solar masses) in a late evolutionary phase characterized by alternating hydrogen- and helium-shell burning around an electron-degenerate carbon–oxygen core. After each helium-shell flash (thermal pulse), the convective envelope of the star may penetrate inward into layers previously processed by nuclear burning, dredging freshly synthesized elements (notably ^12C and s-process elements) to the surface. This mixing event is called the third dredge-up (3DU).

The physical region where 3DU occurs presents a sharp discontinuity in chemical composition and in the radiative opacity κ between the H-rich convective envelope and the underlying He/C-rich intershell. Standard one-dimensional stellar evolution models describe convection through local prescriptions (such as mixing-length theory) supplemented by ad hoc criteria for the convective boundary (Schwarzschild or Ledoux), and treat penetration/overshooting beyond the formal boundary by parameterized algorithms. As a consequence, in current fully evolutionary AGB codes, the depth and efficiency of the 3DU is set by one or more tunable free parameters (e.g. an overshooting length, a minimum core mass for dredge-up, or a dredge-up efficiency parameter λ).

Problem. Formulate, from first physical principles, a treatment of convection and convective–radiative boundary mixing in a 1D stellar evolution framework that:

(i) correctly handles turbulent mixing across an interface with simultaneous strong gradients in mean molecular weight μ and opacity κ;
(ii) determines the location and motion of the convective boundary, and the resulting chemical mixing profile, without invoking arbitrary parameterizations or freely adjustable efficiency parameters; and
(iii) when applied through a sequence of thermal pulses on the TPAGB, predicts the depth and chemical yield of each third dredge-up episode as a deterministic outcome of the equations governing the stellar structure, hydrodynamics, and microphysics.

Provide such a treatment, prove that it reduces to known limits in regimes without composition/opacity discontinuities, and demonstrate that the resulting 3DU efficiency λ (defined as the ratio of the mass dredged up to the mass by which the H-exhausted core grew during the preceding interpulse) is fixed uniquely by the stellar parameters (mass, metallicity, evolutionary state) with no free tuning.
artifact.status_search_result: The treatment of convective boundary mixing during the third dredge-up in TPAGB stars remains an open modeling problem. Recent reviews and papers (e.g., Karakas & Lattanzio 2014; Cinquegrana & Karakas 2022; 3D hydrodynamic simulations by Freytag, Herwig, and collaborators through the mid-2020s) continue to report that 1D AGB evolution codes use parameterized overshooting or dredge-up efficiency parameters, and that a fully first-principles description of mixing across the composition/opacity discontinuity at the base of the convective envelope is still lacking.

status_evidence.title: The Dawes Review 2: Nucleosynthesis and Stellar Yields of Low- and Intermediate-Mass Single Stars (Karakas & Lattanzio)
status_evidence.snippet: The depth of the third dredge-up and its efficiency remain highly uncertain and are typically parameterized in 1D stellar evolution codes via overshooting or efficiency parameters.
status_evidence.claim: The 3DU efficiency in AGB models is still controlled by free parameters.

status_evidence.title: Convective boundary mixing in AGB stars (Herwig et al., 3D hydrodynamics)
status_evidence.snippet: 3D hydrodynamic simulations of the convective envelope–intershell interface in AGB stars indicate complex mixing not captured by standard MLT, and a complete first-principles 1D prescription is not yet available.
status_evidence.claim: A first-principles treatment of mixing across the H/He discontinuity in TPAGB stars is still under active investigation.
